newsitem.title: CHINA: China listed firms step up takeovers.
newsitem.headline: China listed firms step up takeovers.

text.p: China's listed firms are taking over increasing numbers of unlisted firms, partly under orders from Beijing to help get rid of the huge number of loss-making state-run companies, analysts said on Wednesday.

Such takeovers, called "asset re-organisation" in the official media, will be a significant focus of activity by listed companies in the coming years as China continues efforts to restructure its ailing state sector, they said.
Six takeovers have been announced in the past two months by companies listed on the Shanghai stock exchange alone.
They include the acquisition by Shanghai Petrochemical Co of the Jinyang Acrylic Fibres Plant in Shanghai and Shanghai Jinling Co's takeover of the Shanghai Mini-electronics Plant.

"In the past a few years, the central government has urged well-run firms including listed firms to take over loss-making state-run enterprises, promising a package of preferential measures," said an analyst with Shenyin & Wanguo Securities.
"This is partly a reflection of the reluctance of the state to let many state firms declare bankruptcy."
